Subject: Clarify Redwood default retention for requests/outputs (procurement evidence)

Hi Tessa,

Procurement & InfoSec at BrightBank are asking us to confirm what Redwood keeps by default for API interactions. They want concise language we can include in our vendor packet covering:

- What Redwood stores by default for a Hosted API customer: requests (user prompts), model outputs, and any intermediate/streamed tokens
- Retention horizon for each class (how long data is retained before auto-delete)
- How customers can request deletion / what evidence is provided back to the customer
- Exceptions (exports, support artifacts, audit logs, legal holds) and estimated timelines

Can you provide an evidence-ready response (short bullets + one-paragraph summary) and attach any SOC2 or erasure runbook artifacts we can hand to procurement? They prefer a one-page summary for the packet followed by a technical annex.

Thanks — we need this by EOD Friday so procurement can include it in next week's review.

Best,

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Clarify Redwood default retention for requests/outputs (procurement evidence)

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise, procurement-friendly summary followed by a short technical annex. I attached a one-page SOC2 summary and our erasure_runbook_v1.md (runbook is an operational artifact — highlights included).

Executive summary (to include in packet):
- Default capture: For Hosted API customers, Redwood retains API requests (user inputs/prompts) and final model responses (outputs) by default for 45 days to support debugging, quality monitoring, and abuse detection. Streamed token fragments are treated as transient buffers and are not persisted unless the stream finalizes into a saved output.
- Derived artifacts: Model-derived embeddings, vectors, and user-created artifacts are retained per the customer's configuration; defaults may vary based on product (embeddings vs. chat session exports).
- Deletion / erasure: Customers can request account-level erasure via our support portal or via their account rep. For Hosted customers, we complete request-level erasure within 3 business days for raw request/response records and provide a timestamped erasure certificate. Derived artifacts (indexes, aggregated analytics) may require a separate purge (up to 10 business days). Dedicated/Private customers can configure retention windows or manage deletion locally.
- Exceptions & holds: Exports created by customers, tickets created for support, and audit logs required for compliance are retained per their specific processes (audit logs: 90 days by default). Legal holds override auto-delete; we surface a record of the hold and the associated tombstone once resolved.

Technical annex (brief):
- What counts as "request": full user payload sent in the HTTP body (including metadata). "Response": full final completion returned by the model. Streaming buffers are buffered in memory and dropped unless a finalization event writes them to storage.
- Storage & residency: For Hosted, data resides in the region selected on the account (US/EU/APAC); we keep metadata indices for routing and billing longer (30–90 days) for operational reasons, but the request/response content follows the 45-day rule by default. For Private deployments, customers can adopt their own retention and KMS (HSM) controls.
- Erasure evidence: We provide an automated erasure certificate (ISO timestamp, object IDs removed, and verification token). For higher-compliance needs we can provide a scoped export of tombstone records and a signed attestation from our Security team.
- How to opt-out of capture: Customers can set an API flag (x-redwood-no-store: true) on requests to mark them ephemeral; we honor this for Hosted plans where applicable and it prevents storage of request/response content. Note: using the flag may limit debugging/quality support.

CC'ing Kim and Dev for any legal/infra clarifications I missed. If this format works, I can drop the one-page summary into a PDF for procurement.

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Elena / Tessa — quick legal/operational clarifications inline:

> "Default capture: ... retains ... for 45 days"
- Confirmed for Hosted API: 45 days default for request+final response content. For Dedicated customers we offer configurable retention windows (can be set to 0 days for request storage subject to contract).

> "Audit logs: 90 days by default"
- We store operational audit logs (who accessed what in the control plane) for 90 days by default. Audit logs may contain metadata references (request IDs) but not full request payloads unless explicitly exported during support troubleshooting.

> "Erasure timeline: 3 business days / 10 business days for derived artifacts"
- Operationally: we intake erasure requests via support ticketing (or signed request via account rep). The lifecycle is: intake -> identify objects -> run purge -> produce erasure certificate. Hosted: typical SLA is 3 business days for primary objects, up to 10 days for indexes/aggregates. If a legal hold exists we will notify the requestor and pause purge until the hold is released.

> Evidence & artifacts
- We'll attach the SOC2 summary (redacted) and provide a standard erasure certificate template. For procurement, if BrightBank requires a signed attestation, we can route that through Security (DocuSign link included).

I've attached the current erasure_runbook_v1.md (operational) and a short template for the erasure certificate. If you need stronger wording for contract language (e.g., a data-processing addendum paragraph), let us know and we'll get Legal to draft.

—Kim
